Which of the following correctly expresses $T$ as the subject of $B = 2\pi\left(R + \frac{T}{2}\right)$?

$\text{A. } T = \frac{B}{\pi} - 2R$
$\text{B. } T = \frac{B}{\pi} - R$
$\text{C. } T = 2R - \frac{B}{\pi}$
$\text{D. } T = \frac{B}{4\pi} - \frac{R}{2}$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}B&=2\pi\left(R+\frac{T}{2}\right)\\\frac{B}{2\pi}&=R+\frac{T}{2}\\\frac{B}{2\pi}-R&=\frac{T}{2}\\T&=\frac{B}{\pi}-2R\end{aligned}$$
The correct option is A.

B is not valid because $R$ must be doubled when multiplying $\frac{T}{2}$'s equation by 2, so it should be $2R$, not $R$. C has the wrong sign overall, since it equals $-T$. D equals $\frac{1}{4}\left(\frac{B}{\pi}-2R\right)=\frac{T}{4}$, so it is not $T$.

$$\begin{aligned}T&=2\sqrt{\frac{r^2+1}{3}}\\\frac{T}{2}&=\sqrt{\frac{r^2+1}{3}}\\\frac{T^2}{4}&=\frac{r^2+1}{3}\\\frac{3T^2}{4}&=r^2+1\\r^2&=\frac{3T^2}{4}-1\\r&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{3T^2}{4}-1}\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\frac{2x-3}{1-x}\\y(1-x)&=2x-3\\y-xy&=2x-3\\y+3&=2x+xy\\y+3&=x(2+y)\\x&=\frac{y+3}{2+y}\end{aligned}$$
This holds for $y\ne -2$; if $y=-2$, the line $y+3=x(2+y)$ becomes $1=0$, so there is no solution.

content.prompt:
Rearrange the formula below to make $h$ the subject.
Express your answer as a single fraction.
$$a = u \times \sqrt{\frac{p}{kh + x}}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}a&=u\sqrt{\frac{p}{kh+x}}\\\frac{a}{u}&=\sqrt{\frac{p}{kh+x}}\\\frac{a^2}{u^2}&=\frac{p}{kh+x}\\\frac{u^2}{a^2}&=\frac{kh+x}{p}\\\frac{u^2p}{a^2}&=kh+x\\\frac{u^2p}{a^2}-x&=kh\\\frac{u^2p-a^2x}{a^2}&=kh\\h&=\frac{u^2p-a^2x}{a^2k}\end{aligned}$$
Squaring is equivalent here when $a,u,k,p\ne 0$ and $\frac{a}{u}>0$. Otherwise the equation gives no unique real $h$ (no solution, or $h$ not determined).
